::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [1863]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown. This fragment printed in Mary J. Y. Harris, <i>[Memoirs of Frances Mary Peard](other_books/otherbook_318.qmd)</i>, (1903) 48-49.
:::

My [clever woman](cmy_books/cmybook_58.qmd),[^1] instead of living alone as she intended when [you](people/person_1160.qmd) were here, has had a flirtation with three magazines, and is at present engaged to Hogg’s *[Churchman’s Family Magazine](organizations/other_63.qmd)* if she can agree to settlements.

---

[^1]: *The Clever Woman of the Family*. Harris writes of CMY: “No doubt the imaginary people of her own creation were to her as real friends as any others, but to the uninitiated who received her letters this impartiality was a little confusing. Some of her letters preserved by Miss Peard are examples, though not so typical as some others.”
